FIELD NOTE
COASTAL · WALES

DISPATCH #142 — CARDIGAN BAY SALTMARSH TRIAL

Three years on, the Cardigan Bay saltmarsh is holding sediment faster than projected.

Treasurer Aine McAdam and field lead Ruan Hollander walked the C-14 transect on 28 September. Accretion across the breach now averages +18.4 mm/yr — comfortably above the modelled floor of 12 mm/yr — with sparse cordgrass establishing without seeding intervention. Full methodology, sediment cores, and unit costs are attached.

By Ruan Hollander · 02 Oct 2025 · Plot C-14, Aberystwyth · 14 min read

· Watershed

Beaver dam analogues at Glen Lonan: first measurable channel widening.

Eighteen months after install, BDAs 04 through 09 are storing measurable water in the dry-season transect. Mean wetted width up from 1.8m to 3.2m across 240m. Sediment retention behind structure 04 is now ankle-deep on the upstream face.

15 Sep 2025
· Carpathian Trust
· 5 min
From the Carpathian Trust: thirty hectares of old-growth beech now under perpetual protection.

Land parcel 12-B, contiguous with the existing Putna-Vrancea reserve, was transferred to community trust on 11 September. Sable Anchor co-financed the easement at €184/ha — well under the regional average of €310/ha — through the Eastern Carpathians Cluster.

Year-three survival audit, Loch Awe planting: 78.4% across 142,000 stems.

Survey of the 2022 cohort completed mid-August. Sitka spruce removed from the mix in 2023 continues to outperform expectations in the comparison plots; downy birch leading at 91.2% survival, juniper trailing at 54.6% as predicted on the exposed eastern ridge.

Peat re-wetting at Border Mires: water table holding within 8 cm of surface for 142 of 156 monitored days.

The 2024 bunding work across Block 7 has produced the season we hoped for. Dipwells P-001 through P-024 logged hourly; mean depth-to-water sits at -6.4 cm, comfortably inside the IUCN active-restoration band. Methane flux measurements scheduled for October.

Partial blowout on the right bank, repaired in a single day by the Argyll crew. Cost to project: £318 in additional willow material, logged.
